title: Election winner with a majority rule
description: A club elects one officer. There is a list of candidate names (each name appears once) and a list of ballots, each ballot being one text. A ballot is valid when its text is exactly the name of a candidate; every other ballot, including an empty one or one with different letter case, is spoiled and is ignored completely. Write election_winner, which takes the candidates and the ballots and returns the name of the winner. A candidate wins only with a strict majority: more than half of the valid ballots, so exactly half is not enough. Checks happen in this order, and the first failing one decides the result: no candidates at all gives the error "no candidates"; no valid ballots (including an empty ballot list) gives "no valid ballots"; otherwise the candidate with the most votes is found, and if that candidate does not have a strict majority the error is "no majority: " followed by the candidate's name, " leads with ", the candidate's votes, " of " and the number of valid ballots (for example "no majority: ann leads with 2 of 4"). When several candidates share the highest vote count, the leader is the one that comes first in the list of candidates.

args: no majority: ann leads with 1 of 2

notes: Level 2: counting per key without a map, a derived total (valid ballots only), strict majority arithmetic and a tie rule. Pitfalls: the majority is over valid ballots, not over all ballots; exactly half fails; ties for the lead are broken by candidate order, not by ballot order; spoiled ballots are not counted anywhere; with no candidates the error comes before the no-valid-ballots error even when ballots exist.
